purpose: Verify taxonomy-driven diagnosis and minimal preservation-aware repair of common synthetic-image failures.

scoring.pass_condition: Each case must identify the relevant artifact domain, preserve locked content, repair dependencies in the correct order, choose the smallest justified edit scope, and avoid adding unrelated realism tokens.
critical_failures: changing identity, product geometry, pose, composition, wardrobe, text, environment or other locked content without authorization
repairing surface texture before a structural, lighting, contact, shadow or reflection cause
using global regeneration when a local repair is sufficient
adding pores, dirt, scratches, wrinkles, grain, flyaways or asymmetry merely to make the image feel real
calling a reference-conditioned regeneration an exact edit
claiming the image was visually verified when the host could not inspect the result

cases.input_description: Portrait has waxy, uniformly smooth facial skin while the original identity, makeup, expression and lighting are otherwise correct.
expected_repair: match specular response to source light
must_not: add freckles or wrinkles not present

cases.input_description: Hair contains random broken flyaways and strands that detach from the hairstyle, but overall silhouette, color and wind direction are correct.
must_not: add extra volume unrelated to source

cases.input_description: Both eyes have identical bright catchlights even though the key light comes strongly from camera-left and the right eye is partly shadowed.
expected_diagnosis: catchlight geometry inconsistent with source direction
eye specular symmetry inconsistent with lighting
expected_repair: align catchlight intensity and placement with source geometry
retain natural moisture and iris detail

cases.input_description: A heavy wool coat looks like thin plastic; folds ignore body contact and wind direction.
Luxury watch geometry is correct but metal and glass look CG; highlights are too uniform and reflections do not match the studio setup.
expected_repair: surface roughness variation within material logic

cases.input_description: A shoe appears to hover a few millimeters above the pavement and has no convincing weight/contact shadow.
expected_repair: minor compression or occlusion cues if physically appropriate

cases.input_description: A wet road reflects a bright sign that is not present in the scene and reflects the car at an impossible angle.
expected_repair: align car/light reflections with scene geometry

cases.input_description: Subject has two conflicting hard shadows although the scene contains one visible hard sun source and weak sky fill.
expected_repair: weak ambient/occlusion behavior consistent with sky fill
must_not: soften the sun into studio light
add a rim light to justify the second shadow

cases.input_description: Face is bright from camera-right but every visible window and practical is camera-left; there is no plausible source on the right.
expected_repair: align facial key with plausible source or reduce unsupported right-side illumination
must_not: invent an unseen studio key without reason

cases.input_description: Interior window view, face and deep shadows are all equally visible, producing flat local-tone-mapped HDR halos.
expected_repair: allow controlled clipping or density where justified
must_not: force every tonal region to retain equal detail

cases.input_description: Portrait background has a binary cutout blur: the subject edge is razor-sharp and everything one pixel behind is uniformly smeared.
must_not: increase blur simply to hide the artifact

cases.input_description: Image is oversharpened with crunchy halos around hair, pores, fabric and architecture, while geometry/light are otherwise correct.
must_not: add film grain to hide sharpening

cases.input_description: Crowd scene contains repeated identical faces and duplicated jacket folds in several background people.
expected_repair: introduce plausible non-repeating background variation without changing crowd structure
must_not: add dirt/grain instead of fixing duplicates
